chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who is standing in the obligatory prayer and forgets his bag or belongings, fearing their loss or destruction. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He cuts his prayer and secures his belongings, then he resumes the prayer.' I said: 'If he is in the obligatory prayer and an animal escapes from him, or his animal escapes, so he fears it will go away or he will suffer hardship from it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with him cutting his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person break their obligatory prayer to save their belongings from being lost or stolen?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Samaanah, clarifies the juristic principle of 'darar' (harm/loss) in prayer, distinguishing between minor distractions and significant property loss. It establishes that preserving wealth from ruin takes precedence over maintaining the continuity of the obligatory prayer, allowing the worshipper to break, secure the item, and resume. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with practical necessity, ensuring that religious obligations do not lead to undue financial hardship.
